documents.shelfmark: ANTT, Manuscritos da Livraria n.º 1017, letter 153 (PT/TT/MSLIV/1017/00153), f. 153 (scan m0157)

plaintext.source: No decipherment of this letter; the volume's list of deciphered passages (m0276) covers two sibling passages in the same alphabet (Cartas 187 and 212).

transcription.notes: 28 words as first transcribed; l153_reading.txt divides them into 31 words and corrects zfoeE to zfacE from the siblings. Heading on the page says 21 Nov 1644, the date line 21 Sept 1644.

system.summary: Two letter-for-letter substitution alphabets with a few homophones, written as pseudo-words with word divisions kept, plus a symbol for Castile and a code word for the French king: alphabet A in Latin letters (1642-43), alphabet B in Greek-shaped signs (1644-45).
system.sibling_key: Same letter-book: clear copies of letters 8 (Papel junto), 9 and 13 (Carta inclusa) for alphabet A; the volume's list of deciphered passages (m0276) for Cartas 187 and 212 in alphabet B.

prior_solution.where: Contemporary clear copies of letters 9 and 13 in the letter-book, and a contemporary list deciphering Cartas 54, 59, 60, 82, 187 and 212 (m0276). Brice Dudout (email, 27 Oct 2026) had rebuilt alphabet A from the same clear copies (unpublished, key not seen). Laranjo Coelho's 1940-42 edition not seen.

conditions.human_role: Pasted the catalogue 380 task page; no other input.

solution.what: Downloaded the 289 DigitArq scans of MSLIV 1017 through the open JSON API (1060 px; the viewer serves nothing larger).

Aligned the cipher of letter 8 (m0019) with its 'Papel junto' and letter 13 with its 'Carta inclusa': ecinarcinu = sentimento, fxotnc = Duarte, paecico = licença, uxntur = outros. Alphabet A rebuilt (key.py).
Letter 9 transcribed and deciphered with key.py, checked against its clear copy on m0021: 149 of 158 words read.
Letter 13 transcribed and deciphered, checked word by word against the Carta inclusa: 199 of 207 legible words read; faint lines on m0025 left [..].
Letters of 9 Oct and 20 Nov 1643 (44, 49, 56) located on m0064-m0068 and m0085; key unchanged; 24 of 42 transcribed words read, the rest illegible at the scan resolution.
Letter 153 (m0157) transcribed: 28 words, 148 letters, 21 signs, a second alphabet with Greek-shaped signs.
Alphabet A and every shift of it applied to letter 153.
Homophonic hill climb, one-to-one anneal and anneals seeded from short words (p=e, E=m) on letter 153, pt-modern order 5 with spaces.
Swept all 289 scans: two more passages in alphabet B (m0179, 14 Jan 1645; m0190, 7 Feb 1645) and the volume's list of deciphered passages on m0276, which gives both in clear.
Alphabet B rebuilt from the m0276 clear text against m0179 and m0190 (imfeqtix = principe, zfacE = filho, ixmxfmq = Pereira).

Letter 153 deciphered with alphabet B: the marriages of Prince Teodósio and the Infantas, not to be confided to the marquês de Cascais or anyone else; 26 of 31 words read, 4 words before 'mandado' and one after it open.

Statistical validation (docs/_validate.py): 1164 tokens, 20 types, pt-modern order 4: reading -2.508 per letter; random keys -7.09 (z 6.9); key annealed onto shuffled ciphertext best -4.213 (mean -4.283, z 27.7); annealer on the real text -2.472. Verdict: pass.

validation.notes: claimed per-occurrence score -2.508; polyphony 0.0; 0 unread tokens left out; annealer on the real text from random keys reached -2.472

outcome.method: key recovered based on adjacent plaintext
outcome.method_basis: Both alphabets rebuilt from clear text in the same letter-book: the clear copies of letters 8, 9 and 13 (alphabet A) and the volume's list of deciphered passages for two 1645 siblings (alphabet B).
outcome.fraction_read_source: transcription_l09/l13/l44/l49/l56.txt counts and l153_reading.txt: 398 of 438 transcribed cipher words read; untranscribed illegible words not counted

texts.label: Letter 9, 28 Dec 1642
texts.summary: The release of the Infante D. Duarte: the French king's letters to Prince Thomas and Longueville to intercept his escort to Milan, Spanish prisoners of rank to be exchanged for him, force or flight too dangerous for his life, secrecy essential.

reading_review.note: Read as sentences against the clear copy: coherent Portuguese throughout; holes are one blotted name and a few doubtful words.

texts.label: Letter 13, 31 Dec 1642
texts.summary: French ships licensed for Madagascar; Richelieu reported dead, the man who most fomented the war with Castile; Nisa to penetrate the secrets of Castile and of the French court.

reading_review.note: Runs A-C read as coherent sentences matching the Carta inclusa; run D is mostly illegible on the scan and given from the clear copy.

texts.label: Letters 44, 49 and 56, 9 Oct and 20 Nov 1643
texts.summary: Short cipher runs inside clear letters: the congress of Münster, news of the Infante from Genoa, the instructions of France and Castile for the general peace.

reading_review.note: Fragments: the legible words form phrases that fit the clear context; most words of the runs are illegible at 1060 px.

texts.label: Letter 153, 21 Sept 1644
texts.summary: The marriages of Prince Teodósio and the Infantas are not to be confided to the marquês de Cascais or anyone else.

reading_review.note: Two coherent clauses in Portuguese, matching the 1645 sibling passage on the same subject; five words at the end unread.
